title: Meatloaf
subtitle: Ketchup-glazed beef and pork loaf baked in a tin
excerpt: Meatloaf is a mixture of beef mince, pork mince, egg, breadcrumbs, and aromatics packed into a loaf tin and baked under a sticky ketchup glaze. It slices cleanly when cold and makes good sandwiches the next day. The ketchup glaze caramelises in the oven to a lacquered finish.
sourceNotes: American domestic tradition. Meatloaf appears in Fannie Farmer, The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896), Project Gutenberg, and in WPA-era American state-cookery surveys of the 1930s. The ketchup-glaze version became the standard mid-century presentation.

recipe.freezeNotes: Slice the cooked, cooled meatloaf and freeze portions between sheets of baking paper. Reheat slices in a covered pan with a splash of beef stock.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Meatloaf is best made the day before: bake it, cool it in the tin, then refrigerate overnight. It slices more cleanly when cold and reheats well.

glossaryTerms.definition: A paste of bread or breadcrumbs soaked in milk or stock, added to meat mixtures such as meatloaf or meatballs to keep them moist and tender during cooking.

content.text: Meatloaf is a mixture of beef and pork mince bound with egg and a

of breadcrumbs soaked in milk, baked in a loaf tin at 180°C with a ketchup glaze on top. The pork keeps it moist where beef alone would dry out. Softened onion and celery in the base carry the flavour.

items.prepNote: finely chopped and softened in butter

content.text: Melt a knob of butter in the frying pan over medium heat. Add the {{onion}} onion and {{celery}} celery stalks. Cook for 6 minutes until soft. Add {{garlic}} of garlic and cook for 1 minute more. Set aside to cool.

Soak {{breadcrumbs-fresh}} of fresh breadcrumbs in {{whole-milk}} of milk for 2 minutes. In a large bowl, mix {{beef-mince}} of beef mince, {{pork-mince}} of pork mince, the soaked breadcrumbs, and the cooled onion mix. Add the 2 beaten eggs, {{worcestershire-sauce}} of Worcester sauce, {{mustard-powder}} of mustard powder, {{thyme-dried}} of dried thyme, salt, and pepper.

Mix until combined but do not overwork it. Press into a lined 2 lb (900 g) loaf tin. Mix together the {{ketchup}} of ketchup, {{light-brown-sugar}} of brown sugar, and {{cider-vinegar}} of vinegar for the glaze. Spread half over the top.

Heat the oven to 180°C. Bake for 45 minutes. Spread the rest of the glaze over the top. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes more until the glaze is dark and sticky and a probe reads 70°C at the centre. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

items.cause: Not enough binder (egg and breadcrumb) or sliced while still hot.
items.fix: Rest for at least 10 minutes before cutting. For the cleanest slices, refrigerate and cut cold.
Use a mix with at least 15% fat. Check the internal temperature rather than relying on time alone: 70°C is done.

items.symptom: Glaze burning before the loaf is cooked
items.cause: Oven too hot, or glaze applied too early.
items.fix: Apply the first half of the glaze at the 45-minute mark, not before. Cover loosely with foil if it is darkening too fast.

items.symptom: Watery liquid pooling in the tin
items.cause: Excess moisture from the onions or mince.
items.fix: Make sure the softened onions are fully cooled and squeeze out any excess moisture. The liquid can be tipped off and reduced into a quick pan sauce.

content.text: All-beef meatloaf is leaner and needs more moisture: add an extra egg. Stuffed meatloaf has a layer of sliced hard-boiled eggs or a filling of spinach and cheese rolled into the centre before baking. A glaze of brown sauce in place of ketchup gives a British-diner version.

Meatloaf is the quintessential American Sunday-dinner dish, a stretch meal that turns a modest amount of mince into a centrepiece for six. Its reputation for domesticity and frugality is exactly right. Cold meatloaf in a sandwich the next day is considered by many the better version.
